clue.text: Country where old emperor follows the French

parts.note: les is the French plural word for 'the'
Otho was a Roman emperor in AD 69, the Year of the Four Emperors

explanation.surface: A travel question about a land where an ancient ruler succeeded French royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' needs no reordering here, since the French article already comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a small kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Louisiana trial is delayed more than all others

parts.note: LA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Louisiana
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A court case in Louisiana has been postponed longer than any other.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of late describes whatever comes after every rival, so most delayed of all.

clue.text: Teacake colleague left wrapped in paper, with note

indicators.note: the colleague and left go inside the paper's name, which closes round them like wrapping

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
an ally is a colleague or associate
N is short for note in some crossword usage (as in banknote abbreviations)

explanation.surface: A coworker hands over a teacake still in its newspaper wrapping, with a little message.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sally Lunn is a large light teacake associated with Bath in England; 'paper' is the tabloid name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sally Lunn is a sweet yeast bun traditionally served sliced and buttered with tea.

clue.text: The pool swimming is first-rate

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters moving about freely, as if in the water

explanation.surface: The local swimming baths are excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges THEPOOL. Top-hole is dated British slang for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-hole is old-fashioned upper-class British slang meaning excellent or splendid.

clue.text: Missing part of flight is not with the rest

parts.note: if something is missing you are out of it
a step is one stair in a flight of stairs

explanation.surface: A traveller who missed one leg of an air journey is separated from the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel but means a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of step means not keeping pace or in line with everyone else, an idiom from marching.

clue.text: Posh ate here on a trip

definitions.text: Posh ate here on a trip

indicators.note: being on a trip suggests being disoriented, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A society type stopped for refreshments at this place while touring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a trip' rearranges POSHATE; the whole clue then describes where a smart traveller might stop for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea shop is a cafe where travellers might stop for refreshments during an excursion.

clue.text: Tony wild about Right's attempt to deceive

indicators.note: about means going around something, so the scrambled name surrounds the letter
wild suggests the letters running out of control into a new order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A man named Tony is furious about a right-winger's scheme to trick people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' turns TONY into TYON, and 'about' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A try-on is British informal for a bold attempt to get away with something or fool someone.

clue.text: Currency needed if Ghana's to reform

indicators.note: reforming means shaping again, so these letters take on a new arrangement

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Economic advice that Ghana must restructure if it wants a sound currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges IFGHANA; the possessive 's adds no letter. The afghani is the currency of Afghanistan, not Ghana.
explanation.definitionFit: The afghani is the monetary unit used in Afghanistan, so a form of money.

clue.text: Attend prelude for the organ

parts.note: to attend to someone can mean to hear or listen to them

indicators.note: a prelude comes at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: An invitation to a recital: come along to hear the opening piece on the organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the church instrument, but the answer is the body organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart is the muscular body organ that pumps blood round the circulation.

clue.text: End of address is time to parody in attitude of pretence

indicators.note: in places the time and parody inside the word for the pretending attitude

parts.note: a pose is an affected attitude adopted to impress
cod is British slang for a mock or parody, as in a cod accent

explanation.surface: Writing the closing lines of a letter becomes a moment for mockery in an affected manner.
explanation.walkthrough: A UK postcode is written as the last line of a postal address; 'cod' meaning mock is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: On British mail the postal code is written as the final line of the address.

clue.text: Strange sense of remoteness

parts.note: read literally, a paranormal faculty of feeling things at a distance, from Greek words for far and feeling

explanation.surface: Someone describes an odd feeling of being far away.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests detachment or loneliness; the cryptic reading is a strange 'sense' that works over distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Telepathy is supposed mind-to-mind communication across distance, an uncanny faculty beyond the normal five.

clue.text: Balloon, say, such as one might hold at party

definitions.meaning: a balloon is a large rounded brandy goblet, an example of a drinking vessel

definitions.text: such as one might hold at party
definitions.meaning: guests at a party typically hold a drink in a tumbler or wine vessel

explanation.surface: At a party someone holds a balloon, or perhaps something to drink from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balloon' suggests a party decoration but here is a kind of brandy goblet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings name a drinking vessel: a balloon goblet, and the tumbler a party guest holds.

clue.text: Mere assertion signifies nothing

parts.note: to signify something is to say it
O resembles zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A bare claim, unsupported, means nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's say-so is their unsupported word, an assertion offered without proof.

clue.text: Wild supporter with Tory leader has a good man in charge

parts.note: a fan is a supporter, as of a team

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so the first letter of the party word is taken

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is a crossword standard for a good man

explanation.surface: An excited fan, backed by the Conservative chief, has a virtuous person running things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic can mean wildly imaginative or extravagant, beyond the bounds of reality.

clue.text: Badly set Danish Blue is not yet running

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters set down wrongly and needing rearrangement

explanation.surface: A Danish Blue cheese that has been poorly set is not yet ready for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges SETDANISHBLUE (13 letters).
explanation.definitionFit: Something unestablished has not been set up or put into operation yet, so it is not functioning.

clue.text: Not seeing where sheep might be closed in at one end?

definitions.meaning: with eyes covered, unable to see

definitions.text: where sheep might be closed in at one end?
definitions.meaning: a ..., a sheep pen closed off like a blind alley with only one way in

explanation.surface: A shepherd who cannot see wonders where the flock is penned in at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: A blind alley is closed at one end, so a 'blind' fold would be a sheep enclosure shut at one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Blindfold as an adjective describes someone with eyes covered, unable to see anything.

clue.text: Part of mount on which angels are sometimes seen

definitions.meaning: the upper side of a riding animal, where the rider sits

definitions.text: on which angels are sometimes seen
definitions.meaning: angels on ... is a savoury of oysters wrapped in bacon

explanation.surface: A religious image of angels riding on part of a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angels on horseback' is a British savoury of oysters rolled in bacon on toast; 'mount' is a steed, not a mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: The top of a ridden steed is the part a rider mounts and sits upon.

clue.text: One very invigorating sort of muscle action

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
so means very, as in so good
a tonic is something that invigorates or restores

explanation.surface: A single, highly energising kind of muscle exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invigorating' looks like an adjective but supplies the noun for a restorative.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotonic describes muscle contraction in which tension stays constant while the muscle shortens.

clue.text: Brush turkey? Somewhat better than that

definitions.text: Brush turkey? Somewhat better than that

parts.words: Brush turkey? Somewhat better than that
parts.note: a turkey is a flop, so a brush turkey is a hopeless painter; one a little better is an amateur painting at weekends

explanation.surface: A naturalist's note about an Australian bird, and something slightly superior to it.
explanation.walkthrough: A brush turkey is an Australian bird, but 'turkey' also means a failure and 'brush' a painter's tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sunday painter is an amateur who paints for pleasure in spare time, not a professional.

clue.text: Walk hesitatingly with snake on surface of path

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so the snake comes first

parts.note: the asp is a venomous snake
to halt is an old word for to limp or walk unsteadily

explanation.surface: Someone limps along with a snake lying on the path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. Halt as a verb for limping survives mainly in older English.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalt is a tarry material laid as the paving on roads and walkways.

clue.text: Furniture with gold picture that's striking

parts.note: a table is an item of furniture
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A gilded table makes a vivid scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a striking, picturesque scene or group, like a still composed image.

clue.text: Ill-temper experienced about platoon

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for experienced goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: something seen has been witnessed or experienced
PL is the military abbreviation for platoon

explanation.surface: Bad temper witnessed in an army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'experienced' looks like an adjective for skilled, but here means witnessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Spleen means bad temper or spite, from the old belief that the organ caused moodiness.

clue.text: Blast eccentric winner at the table?

parts.note: to trump is to sound a trumpet blast
a card is an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.surface: A loud noise from a peculiar person at the dinner table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the table' suggests dining but means a card table; the question mark flags the hint.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games a card of the trump suit beats any other, a winning play.

clue.text: Black spot one's eradicated in Italian region

indicators.note: eradicated means wiped out, so the letter for one is removed

parts.note: Umbria is a region of central Italy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A dark mark disappears from an Italian region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbra is the darkest central part of a shadow or of a sunspot.

clue.text: A man nowadays further on

parts.note: he is a pronoun for a man
AD, Anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: A modern man who is more advanced.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahead means in front or further forward in position or progress.

clue.text: Noise of alarm note gets slumber out of head

parts.note: B is a musical note

indicators.note: the word for slumber loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: slumber means sleep

explanation.surface: A ringing tone wakes someone from a doze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleep is the short high electronic beep of a pager or alarm.

clue.text: Old African state overthrown through Masai bungling

indicators.note: overthrown means turned over, so the run of letters reads backwards
through points to the letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: An ancient African kingdom toppled because of mismanagement by the Masai.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' finds AIBUN in 'mAsAI BUNgling', and 'overthrown' reverses it. 'bungling' looks like an anagram signal but is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Nubia was an ancient region and kingdom along the Nile, in present Sudan and southern Egypt.

clue.text: Free of duty, excluding levy on single person

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the levy follows the single person

parts.note: ex means without or excluding, as in ex dividend
one is a single person
a rate is a local tax or levy

explanation.surface: Tax exemption excluding a charge on a single householder.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were a British local property tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to release someone from a duty or obligation, or from blame.

clue.text: Spoke caught in headgear

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
someone in headgear is hatted

explanation.surface: A man in a hat spoke after being trapped.
explanation.definitionFit: To have chatted is to have talked informally, a past-tense synonym of spoke.

clue.text: It may be stoned and stewed and bottled or canned

definitions.text: It may be stoned and stewed and bottled or canned

parts.words: It may be stoned and stewed and bottled or canned
parts.note: stoned, stewed, bottled and canned look like ways to prepare fruit, but each is slang for being inebriated

explanation.surface: A recipe note about fruit that can be pitted, cooked and preserved.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as fruit preserving; all four verbs are also slang for being intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Drunken describes someone intoxicated, which all the slang terms in the clue mean.
